its: of it

changes: change, for one thing

only: and no other; not more than
until: while not

between: after one thing and before an other thing
ignore: not use
ignores: ignore, for one thing
many: more than two
equals: is equal to
which: what one
whose: of which
there: at that place
any: one or more, or all; it is not a known one
cannot: can not
must: has to
may: can; it is not always so
want: have a need for
ways: more than one way
them: the things before; more than one it
they: the things before, as the one that does a thing
these: this, for more than one thing
but: and not as you can know from the words before
few: not many
made: what you make
done: what you do
on: in use; at the place of

running: a program is running from when you run it to its end
go: change the place where a thing is

back: to the place before
fact: a thing that is true
about: of; with a rule or a fact on it
facts: more than one fact
reference: a file that says the rules of a language and how to use each part of it
outside: not in
rest: the part that is not used
yet: before now
try: test if you can
find: get to know where a thing is
stop: end; not run more

waits: wait, for one thing
kind: a set of things that are the same in some way
names: more than one name
files: more than one file
programs: more than one program
functions: more than one function
like: the same in some way as
too: also
four: three and one

six: five and one
seven: six and one
eight: seven and one
nine: eight and one
ten: nine and one
sixteen: ten and six
negative: a number is negative when it is less than zero
positive: a number is positive when it is more than zero
absolute: the absolute value of a number is that number, or zero subtract that number when it is negative
power: a number to the power three is that number times that number times that number
remainder: the part of a number you can not divide: seven divide by two has a remainder of one
exponent: a number that says how many times to multiply by ten; with a negative exponent, you divide by ten
integer: a whole number; it can be negative
integers: more than one integer
fractional: the fractional part of a number is the part after the point
maximum: the value that is more than each other value
minimum: the value that is less than each other value
mark: a thing you write that is not a word
marks: more than one mark
letter: a mark that can be a part of a word
letters: more than one letter
digit: a mark that says one number from zero to nine

digits: more than one digit
precision: the count of digits the computer keeps in the result of maths
round: make a number have less digits; if the first digit you take away is five or more, add one to the last digit you keep
rounded: what you get when you round
truncate: make a number have less digits after the point, and do not round
character: one letter, one digit, or one other mark; the computer can store it in memory
characters: more than one character
string: a list of characters in order; a string can have no characters
strings: more than one string
text: words as data; text is a string
blank: the character you put between two words; it is not a letter and not a digit
blanks: more than one blank
empty: a string is empty when it has no characters
null: empty; a null string has no characters
length: the count of characters in a string
short: with a length that is less
position: a number that says where a character is in a string; the first character is at position one
positions: more than one position
left: the start of a string; the part at the first positions
right: the end of a string; the part at the last positions
pad: a character you put in a string so the string has the length you want
upper: one of the two ways each letter can be; a word in upper is in this way: WORD
lower: the other of the two ways each letter can be; a word in lower is in this way: word
caseless: a compare is caseless when a letter in upper and the same letter in lower are equal
quote: the name of a mark; a string in code can start and end with it
literal: a string in code, put between two quote marks; its value is the characters between the marks
decimal: a way to write a number with the digits zero to nine
hexadecimal: a way to write a number with sixteen digits: the digits zero to nine, then six letters
binary: a way to write a number with only the digits zero and one
bit: one binary digit
bits: more than one bit
byte: eight bits; one character is one byte
bytes: more than one byte
sign: the mark before a negative number; a number that is not negative has no sign
comma: the name of a mark; you put it between two values in a list
colon: the name of a mark
slash: the name of a mark
star: the name of a mark
dash: the name of a mark
exclamation: the name of a mark
question: a thing you say when you want to know a thing; also the name of a mark
underscore: the name of a mark
parentheses: the name of two marks; they start and end a part of code
special: not the same as the other things of a set
rexx: a language for programs; it has few rules, and its values are strings

open: you can read and change open code
object: a thing in memory that has data and has a set of functions it can run
objects: more than one object
class: a thing that makes objects; each object a class makes has the functions of that class
classes: more than one class
oorexx: open object rexx; the rexx language with objects and classes; these parts are about it
line: a part of a file or a part of text; the end of one line is the start of the next line
semicolon: the name of a mark; it can end a step of code in the middle of a line
lines: more than one line
clause: one step of rexx code; a clause ends at the end of a line, or at a semicolon
clauses: more than one clause
instruction: one clause that the language has a rule for, as say or if
instructions: more than one instruction
keyword: a word that starts an instruction or is a part of an instruction; the word is not a variable there
keywords: more than one keyword
symbol: a word in code made of letters, digits, and the marks point, exclamation, question, and underscore; it can be the name of a variable
symbols: more than one symbol
constant: a value that can not change; a constant symbol starts with a digit or a point
expression: code that gives a value when it runs
operator: a mark or marks in an expression that say what to do with the values next to it, as add or compare
operators: more than one operator
token: one part of a clause: a literal, a symbol, a number, an operator, or a special mark
tokens: more than one token
expressions: more than one expression
operand: a value next to an operator
operands: more than one operand
variables: more than one variable
assign: put a value in a variable
assigns: assign, for one thing
assignment: a clause that assigns a value to a variable
assigned: a variable is assigned when it has a value
uninitialized: a variable is uninitialized when no value is assigned to it
drop: make a variable have no value; then it is uninitialized
comment: text in code that the computer does not run; it starts with a slash and a star and ends with a star and a slash, or it starts with two dash marks and ends at the end of the line
shell: a program that reads strings of text from you and runs them as programs
command: a string that a rexx program gives to an other program, as a shell, to run
commands: more than one command
environment: the name of the program that gets each command; also, the place where names are known
routine: a part of a program that has a name and that you can call; it can give a result
routines: more than one routine
subroutine: a routine that you call with the call instruction; it does not have to give a result
internal: in this program file
external: not in this program file
builtin: a builtin function is a part of the language; you do not have to write it
method: a function that an object can run; it has a name
methods: more than one method
argument: a value you give to a function, a routine, or a method when you call it
arguments: more than one argument
optional: an argument is optional when you do not have to give it
omit: not give; you can omit an optional argument
omitted: an omitted argument is one you do not give
default: the value a thing has if you do not give a value
option: a word or a letter you give as an argument, to say the way you want a thing to be done
options: more than one option
procedure: an instruction that makes the variables of a routine not known to the other parts of the program
pool: the set of variables that a part of a program can use
local: known only in one part of a program
global: known in all parts of a program
label: a symbol with a colon after it, at the start of a clause; a call can go to it
labels: more than one label
come: go to here
signal: an instruction that goes to a label and does not come back
directive: a clause that starts with two colon marks; it is not a step that runs; it says a rule of the code, as where a class or a method starts
directives: more than one directive
package: a file of rexx code with its routines, classes, and directives
packages: more than one package
public: known to code in other packages
private: known only in the same class or package
stem: a symbol whose last character is a point; one stem can have many values
stems: more than one stem
tail: the part of a symbol after the first point
compound: a compound symbol is a stem and a tail
group: a list of clauses that run as one
nested: a thing is nested when it is in an other thing of the same kind
event: a thing that is true at one time when a program runs, as an error
events: more than one event
trap: a part of a program that runs when an event is true
traps: more than one trap
raise: make an event true, so a trap can run
raised: an event is raised when you raise it
exit: end the whole program
leave: end a loop and run the clause after it
halt: stop a program from the outside
trace: a list of each clause a program runs, with values; you read it to find an error
debug: find and change an error in a program
interactive: a program is interactive when it stops and waits for you to say what to do next

message: what you give an object to make it run a method; a message has the name of a method and the arguments
messages: more than one message
send: give a message to an object
sends: send, for one thing
sent: a message is sent when you send it
receiver: the object you send a message to
instance: an object that a class makes
instances: more than one instance
subclass: a class that has all the methods of an other class, and can have more methods
subclasses: more than one subclass
superclass: the other class of a subclass
inherit: a subclass can inherit the methods of its superclass: it has them and can use them
inherits: inherit, for one thing
mixin: a class that gives methods to other classes, but is not the superclass of them
metaclass: a class whose instances are classes
attribute: a value of an object that methods can get and set
attributes: more than one attribute
expose: a method can expose a variable of its object; then the method can use and change that variable
exposed: a variable is exposed when a method can use it by expose
self: the object that runs the method now
super: the superclass of the class of the method that runs now
new: not there before; the new method makes a new instance of a class
init: the method that a class runs when it makes a new instance
scope: the class a method is a part of; a method can use only the variables of its scope
collection: an object that has other objects in it
item: one object in a collection
items: more than one item
collections: more than one collection
index: a value that says where an item is in a collection
indexes: more than one index
array: a collection in order, where each index is a whole number from one
arrays: more than one array
disk: a part of a computer that keeps files when the computer is off
directory: a collection where each index is a string; also a place on a disk that has files
table: a collection where each index can be any object
supplier: an object that gives each index and item of a collection, one after the other
queue: a list of items or lines; you put an item at the start or at the end, and you take from the start
stream: a file, or the input or the output of a program, that you read from or write to in order
streams: more than one stream
nil: the object that says there is no value; its name is point nil
boolean: a value that is true or false; in rexx, the number one is true and the number zero is false
concurrent: two things are concurrent when they run at the same time
guarded: a method is guarded when only one guarded method of an object can run at a time; the other methods wait
guard: what makes a method guarded
unguarded: a method is unguarded when it can run at the same time as other methods of the same object
activity: one way the computer runs a program; two of them can run at the same time
activities: more than one activity
caller: the part of a program that calls a routine or sends a message
reply: give the result back to the caller, then go on to run the rest of the method
cut: put an end to one part and a start to the next part, so one string is two strings
parse: cut a string in parts and put each part in a variable
template: the part of a parse instruction that says how to cut the string and which variables get the parts
pattern: a string or a position in a template that says where to cut
patterns: more than one pattern
placeholder: a point in a template; it takes a part of the string, but the part goes to no variable
